thread:
zoe: Heads-up for people heading to SplinterConf next week — what are people's weird must-pack items? not laptops, silly stuff.
omar: Compression socks. saved my legs after the red-eye.
claire: Noise-cancelling earplugs + a tiny sleep mask (not the bulky one). makes hotel naps actually work.
ben: A rubber doorstop. Hotels with thin doors = instant peace.
ora: (not coming but chiming in) hotel coffee is always sad / pack instant espresso sachets.
zoe: @omar which compression socks brand?
omar: Bombas running ones are comfy. I buy a neutral color so they look normal on panels.
claire: Pro tip: a little packet of detergent + sink stopper = quick laundry for shirts.
ben: Also, bring a tiny surge strip if you're bringing multiple chargers. Hotels have limited plugs.
travel-bot: FYI: Some international venues require digital vaccine proof — check conference emails before you travel.
maria: Shoe rotation: bring a foldable shoe bag. Saved my suitcase from muddy boots after a hike.
zoe: Anyone have luck with getting early check-in on arrival?
omar: If you're a loyalty member, usually. Otherwise text the front desk 2 hours before landing and offer to pay a small fee — sometimes they honour it.
claire: Another weird one: a mini clothesline + clips. Hotel shower racks are useless for drying chargers and socks.
ben: Food hack: pack a few protein bars and a small reusable spoon. Conference food runs out fast.
zoe: This is gold. Also last-minute: anyone recommend a small travel steamer vs ironing?
maria: Steamer. Way faster and safer on wrinkle-prone shirts.
zoe: Thanks all, I'll assemble a tiny 'conference survival' pack and drop it in #offsite-logistics. :star:
